newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey promises to clean up human rights abuses.
newsitem.headline: Turkey promises to clean up human rights abuses.

text.p: Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller promised on Thursday to clean up Turkey's human rights record, often criticised by Europe and human rights groups.

"We are ready to do everything necessary to bring our country's human rights to the most advanced level," Ciller told a news conference. "We want our people to have human rights of the highest international standards," she said.
Amnesty International launched a worldwide campaign this month to highlight rights abuses in Turkey, including extrajudicial killings, torture and disappearances.
The rights group has criticised Turkey for failing to live up to previous promises to stamp out rights violations.
The European Parliament last month threatened to hold back hundreds of millions of dollars in European Union aid to Turkey, partly because of its rights record.
Ciller said Turkey would decrease the period of detention in custody and make changes to the State Security Court system. She gave few details.
Suspects held under anti-terror laws can be detained for up to a month in ten emergency rule provinces in the mainly-Kurdish southeast and two weeks in the rest of Turkey.
Ciller, a pro-Western conservative in coalition with Islamists, said Europe would have no reason to shun Turkey once its rights performance improved.
"If Europe continues to keep Turkey out it will become a Christian club. That is dangerous for regional and world peace," she said.
